Make vector art 3D in Inkscape

A walk through the Vector 3Dit 3D Editor, one tab at a time. Each lesson uses real screenshots of the editor. The numbered dots on each picture match the steps beside it.

About 15 minutesInkscape 1.2 or newerEverything stays vector

LESSON 01

Open the 3D Editor

  1. Draw a shape in Inkscape, for example a heart, star or circle, and give it a fill color.
  2. Select it. You can select several shapes, or a whole group.
  3. Choose Extensions › Vector 3Dit › 3D Editor…

Not installed yet? Follow the install guide first.

Text? Turn it into shapes first with Path › Object to Path. Text objects are skipped.

While the editor is open, Inkscape waits for it. Click Apply or Cancel to get back to your drawing.

LESSON 02

Find your way around the window

  • 1Kind: Flat, Extrude, Revolve or Inflate. This decides how the flat shape becomes 3D.
  • 2Tabs: View, Shape, Surface, Colors, Light, Outline and Style. Each holds one group of tools.
  • 3Camera: save the view and lock several objects to it, so a whole scene shares one vantage point (lesson 11).
  • 4Trackball: the little cube shows which way the object faces. Drag it to turn.
  • 5Preview: your page, with the objects in 3D exactly where they'll land. The rest of the drawing is faded behind them.
  • 6Preview tools: show or hide the other objects, show them in Full color instead of faded, and zoom to the selection or the whole page.
  • 7Apply writes the result into your drawing. Cancel leaves it unchanged.
LESSON 03 · VIEW TAB

Turn it in space

  1. Drag the cube on the trackball. You can also drag the object in the preview itself.
  2. Or click a preset view. Isometric right is a good start for icons and logos.
  3. Fine-tune with the sliders: Tilt turns around the horizontal axis, Turn around the vertical axis, Spin within the page.

Handy: hold Shift while dragging to turn around one axis only, or Alt to spin flat. Face front resets the rotation. Perspective adds depth like a camera lens; 0 keeps parallel lines parallel.

LESSON 04 · SHAPE TAB

Choose how it becomes 3D

Pick a kind at the top of the panel, then open the Shape tab. It shows only the settings for that kind.

Extrude and bevel

  1. With Extrude picked, set the Depth (up to 1000 px). Turn off Solid for a hollow tube.
  2. Click the Bevel box to open the profiles.
  3. Pick one, like Round. Then set the bevel's width, height and smoothness, front or both sides, inward or outward.

Revolve

  1. Draw half an outline, like half a vase, with its straight side on the left.
  2. Pick Revolve. The shape spins around that edge like clay on a potter's wheel.
  3. Set the Axis to the straight edge. An Angle below 360° cuts it open; Offset makes rings.

Inflate

  1. Pick Inflate to puff the shape up like a balloon.
  2. Puffiness sets the height (up to 1000 px). Profile sets the curve: Round, Pillow, Dome, Soft or Sharp.
  3. Raise Detail for smoother curves (larger files).
LESSON 05 · SURFACE TAB

Pick a material

  1. Click a material swatch. Toon gives flat cel bands and an outline. Chrome, Gold and Copper give a metal look.
  2. Change Shading or Color bands to fine-tune. 2 to 6 bands give a poster look.

Smooth gradients draws curved surfaces with real vector gradients, so rounded shapes look smooth at any size.

LESSON 06 · COLORS TAB

Color each side

  1. Click a color to open the color picker. Front is the shape's own color.
  2. Sides, Bevel and Back follow the front color until you set them. Auto puts them back.
  3. Shadow tone sets the color of the dark sides: tinted, black or your own color.
LESSON 07 · LIGHT TAB

Aim the light

  1. Drag the sun on the sphere to where the light should come from. Drag past the rim to light from behind.
  2. Set Intensity, Ambient (light on every side), Fill light, Highlight and Gloss.
  3. Leave Shared scene light on to give every 3D object in the drawing the same light, so the whole scene matches.
LESSON 08 · OUTLINE TAB

Add lines and a shadow

  1. Edge lines: Outline draws the silhouette and sharp edges. All draws every facet, for a wireframe look.
  2. Shadow: Cast throws a shadow onto the page, away from the light. Floor adds a soft shadow underneath.
  3. Set the shadow's opacity, softness, distance and color.

Lines stay on top. Edge lines are drawn above all the fills, in their own group. A line is hidden only where a face really covers it, so outlines stay crisp.

LESSON 09 · STYLE TAB

Fill, stroke, opacity and names

  1. Fill is the shape's color, the same as Front on the Colors tab.
  2. Stroke draws lines around the 3D object. Pick a color, or None to remove it. Set its width, and whether it draws the outline or every edge.
  3. Opacity makes the whole object see-through.

The color picker: drag in the square for shade, drag the rainbow bar for hue, type a hex code, or click a palette color. Your recent colors show at the top.

Good to know: a shape that already has a stroke in Inkscape keeps it when made 3D. The fill and stroke you set here are saved on the shape, so Remove 3D gives it back with them.

LESSON 09 · STYLE TAB

Every part has a name

The result isn't a pile of anonymous paths: each part is named for what it is, its color and where it sits on the object, like Fill - Light Blue - Front, Fill - Dark Blue - Left Side or Line - Black - Top. Find them under Object › Layers and Objects.

  1. Scroll to Names at the bottom of the Style tab.
  2. Colors as picks Names (Blue, Light Blue, Dark Gray…) or CMYK codes (like C75 M49 Y0 K5), handy for print. A color with no simple name gets its CMYK code either way.

Fills and lines sit in separate Fills and Lines groups, with the shadow in Shadow, so you can select, recolor or hide each kind on its own.

LESSON 10

Groups and several objects

  • Select a group (a logo, for example) and every shape in it becomes 3D. They all turn together around the group's center, so the logo stays in one piece.
  • Select several objects to change them all at once. Only the settings you touch change. Everything else stays as each object has it.
  • Each shape remembers its group's center, so you can later edit one piece alone without it jumping out of place.
LESSON 11 · VIEW TAB

One camera for the whole scene

  1. Select the objects, set up the view, then click Save… next to Camera. Name it, like Street view, choose the page's or the selection's center, and click Save camera.
  2. Add more objects any time: select them and pick the camera from the Camera list.
  3. With Turn on Scene camera, turn any locked object and they all turn together, with the same angles, turning point and perspective, so every line runs to the same vanishing points.

Own view (not locked) unlocks the selection and Delete removes the camera. Unlocked objects keep exactly how they look. Cameras are saved in your Inkscape file.

LESSON 11 · VIEW TAB

Place one object inside the scene

Line objects up without redoing the scene: move just the selection and leave the camera alone.

  1. Select an object that's locked to a camera. The View tab shows Turn: click This object.
  2. Drag the trackball, or use Tilt, Turn and Spin. Only the selection turns, inside the scene.
  3. Drag Push back to move it deeper into the scene, or below 0 to bring it toward you. It shows with Perspective above 0.

Click Scene camera to go back to turning the whole scene. The other objects on the camera never move.

LESSON 12

Apply, edit later, or undo

  • Apply puts the result in your drawing as a group of plain vector shapes, named like 3D Extrude: Heart, with Shadow, Fills and Lines inside. You can move, scale and export it like anything else.
  • Edit it again: select the 3D object and open the 3D Editor. It opens with that object's current settings.
  • Undo: Ctrl+Z in Inkscape undoes the whole Apply in one step.
  • Back to flat: Extensions › Vector 3Dit › Remove 3D puts the original shape back, with its id, fill and stroke.
  • Edit the outline: Remove 3D, reshape the path with Inkscape's tools, then open the 3D Editor again.
  • Detach it for good: ungroup the result and delete the hidden v3d-source path. After that it can't be re-edited.
LESSON 13

Shortcuts in the 3D Editor

Drag the cubeTurn the objects
Shift + dragTurn around one axis only
Alt + dragSpin flat, within the page
← → ↑ ↓Turn in 5° steps (click the cube first)
Scroll on the previewZoom in and out
Right-drag the previewPan around the page
Ctrl+EnterApply
EscCancel and close
